chunks: Were all of you with us in Ṣiffīn?
They replied that some of them were but some of them were not.
Amīr al-mu’minīn said: Then you divide yourselves into two groups. One of those who were in Ṣiffīn and other of those who were not present there, so that I may address each as I see suitable.
Then he shouted to the people: Stop talking and keep quiet to listen to what I say. Turn your hearts to me. Whomever we ask for evidence, he should give it according to his knowledge about it.

key_terms.صِفِّينَ: Siffin, the location of the famous battle between Imam Ali and Muawiyah.

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali distinguish between the Kharijites who witnessed the Battle of Siffin and those who did not?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs a method of epistemological differentiation by separating those who witnessed the Battle of Ṣiffīn from those who did not, ensuring that judgments are based on direct experience rather than hearsay. This stratification highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on contextual knowledge (ʿilm al-ḥāl) in resolving the theological and political dispute over the validity of the arbitration (ḥukm) with Muʿāwiya. By addressing each group according to their specific vantage point, he underscores the principle that authority in religious and political matters must be grounded in accurate, firsthand evidence.
